Resolves #18307

Related: #18304 · #18303 · #18306 (PR #18347) · #18310 (PR #18360) · D#18150 step 1(c)

Header state now has an owner that outlives the commit: the workspace's own `stateProvider`, the workspace-level node of the app's provider hierarchy. `Neo.dashboard.dock.Workspace` carries an engine default (`{module: StateProvider}`); a consumer's own provider on the workspace — the Workstation owns one with its two stores — hosts the same keys beside its own. `HeaderActionPolicy#publishDocument` projects the committed document onto it once per commit under `dock`: `dock.items.<id>.{closable, lockable, locked, pinnable, edge}`, `dock.nodes.<tabsNodeId>.{activeItemId, items}`, `dock.popOutAvailable`, `dock.recreateFallback`; the policy publishes `dock.items.<id>.reloadable` as a pane is resolved and the workspace `dock.flights.<id>` at a reload's or recreate's edges. Every leaf is a `core.Config` that self-diffs. The dock's chrome binds to that truth through the provider's own binding machinery and nothing else: the engine actions the `LayoutAdapter` emits carry the policy's formatters as `bind` (`hidden` / `pressed` / `disabled`); the tab container a tabs node projects into is now the dock's own `interaction/TabContainer`, which binds `dockLockedItemIds` to the node's items and their locks and presents exactly the items whose lock changed — pane `inert`, lock class, tab-button drag token, `dockLock()` delegation, with the policy's exact-restore memory — at construction, on every change, and for a pane the reconciler places later; a `Rail` binds `dockRevealLocked` for the item it reveals and publishes that item itself. Each formatter reads through `getData`, so its `Effect` depends on exactly the leaves it touched. The eleven per-commit dispatch sites in `Workspace.mjs`, the eight `sync*` methods they called, and the boot sweep with its deferral in `afterSetMounted` are gone. Presentation reads state; the mutation path publishes it and re-derives nothing.

Evidence: L2 (unit arms counting executed formatter evaluations per commit; the dashboard/tab unit suites with the lock, pop-out, recreate and boot witnesses re-seamed to bindings) + L3 (the component dashboard suite in a real browser, including the static-boot rig and the async reload single-flight arms; AC-3's permanent Neural Link arm against the running Workstation, run at this head — the e2e tier is Brain-gated, so it runs with the runtime root, not in CI) → L2 required (AC-2 names executed evaluations as the measure). Residual: none.

## AC Evidence

"the engine default provider is created when a consumer supplies none". The sweeps are deleted in the same diff: `Workspace.mjs` calls no `sync*`; `HeaderActionPolicy` has no `syncAll`/`syncActiveItem`/`syncCloseAction`/`syncLockAction`/`syncPinAction`/`syncPopOutAction`/`syncReloadAction`/`syncLockRails` |
| **AC-2** | Same spec, evaluation counts (a policy subclass counting every formatter run, node lock binding included) — "the first paint evaluates each bound formatter once per node; a geometry-only commit evaluates nothing": 8 per node on creation, then `resizeEdgeZone` → **0**; "a lock toggle evaluates exactly the formatters that read the item's lock": `close.hidden`, `dockLockedItemIds`, `lock.pressed` on the one node, the settled refresh adds none; "an activation re-evaluates the header that switched": 7 action formatters on that header, no action formatter elsewhere (a container the reconciler re-parents has its one node binding re-registered by `container.Base#insert` — the framework's re-registration, stated in the arm); "a second workspace's transaction in the same worker evaluates nothing on the first": **0**. Before (at dev, from the #18307 census): every commit ran two settled `syncAll` passes + one post-refresh pass = 3 × (5 syncs × projected tabs) + rails, unconditionally. The zero counts executed formatter evaluations, the measure the AC names; `publishDocument` itself still walks the committed document once per commit — items, tabs nodes, one `findOwningEdge` per item — and its leaves self-diff |
| **AC-3** | `e2e/workstation/WorkstationHeaderStatePopOutNL.spec.mjs` — permanent, Neural Link, run at this head against the running Workstation (receipt in Test Evidence): a real pop-out moves the live `commits` pane into the popup window (same instance, popup `windowId`, mounted); from the popup the pane resolves the same provider it resolved from the opener — the workspace's own, id equal — and reads the item's truth through it (`getState('dock.items.commits')`), equal to what the workspace publishes at that moment. The tear-out is itself a commit (`detachItem` takes the item out of its tabs node), so the one topology-derived field, the owning `edge`, is `null` while the item is out; every other field is unchanged — the arm asserts exactly that. Why the same provider from a viewport that carries none: `component.Abstract#getStateProvider` resolves the closest provider once and keeps it (`closestProvider`), so a pane stays with the workspace whose truth it presents whatever window renders it; the arm pins that engine fact (a hop that reset the resolution would turn it red). `DockHeaderState.spec` pins the single-tree half: actions, panes and workspace resolve one provider |
| **AC-4** | `toolbar.Base#syncActions` untouched (`git diff --stat`: `src/toolbar/` absent) |
| **AC-5** | Component dashboard suite in a real browser (120/121, the one timing arm green 3/3 alone — Test Evidence): `DockLockAction`-family unit arms (lock ↔ unlock on pane, action, close affordance, drag token; delegating `dockLock()` once per transition; live policy replacement inherits restore memory; rail reveal pane both transitions; a fresh projected shell presents its committed lock at construction), `DockActionTooltips` (lock ↔ unlock flips tooltip, icon, accessible name on the retained instance), `DockReload.spec` (single-flight disables the action; per-item; teardown mid-flight — the async DockReload witness preserved: the flight leaf changes header enablement with no document commit), `DockBootSweep.spec` (reload revealed on live chrome after a static boot, from the first paint), `DockWorkspace.spec` (frozen action order, focus-gated reveal, per-pane enablement, host actions untouched by the engine's data, the pin escape and rail return) |

## Deltas from ticket
- **The home is the workspace's own `stateProvider`, chained upward by the ordinary hierarchy — not the Group's provider.** A Workspace's committed document is the unit of header truth; independent roots in one worker must not share item namespaces (Euclid's #18303 boundary); and a single-window app never loads `Neo.manager.Transaction`, so binding to the Group provider would have pulled the manager into every dock consumer's closure. Group-wide truth (`canUndo` / `canRedo`, #18316's actions) binds to PR #18360's Group provider through the manager. The engine's keys live under `dock` so a consumer-owned provider on the workspace hosts them beside its own.
- **Bindings, not effects.** The first cut hand-rolled `core.Effect`s for the lock presentation, with its own lifecycle maps, cleanup and a registration pass; the review (@tobiu) called it a re-implementation of what the provider does, and it was. The lock is now a bound reactive config on dock-owned chrome — `interaction/TabContainer#dockLockedItemIds`, `Rail#dockRevealLocked` — and the framework owns creation, re-evaluation and teardown. `HeaderActionPolicy` imports no `Effect`.
- **Ids travel whole.** The first cut published a tabs node's item list and bound the container's locked-item list as comma-joined strings — a delimiter the document validator does not impose; Euclid's exact-head control (item `a,b`: lock pressed, pane never inert) found it. Both are array leaves now: `core.Config` compares arrays element-wise, so they self-diff like every other leaf, and every id the validator admits presents. Regression arm: an `a,b` item locks, presents and restores. Control at the previous head (probe, not committed): `c.d`, `e f`, `g:h`, `i/j`, `k.locked` and `dock` all presented — full-path leaf keys carry any id; the comma join was the only lossy encoding.
- **`state.Provider#createBinding` pauses dependency tracking around the config assignment.** A component's `afterSet` hooks read sibling configs on their way to the DOM; tracked, those made every binding re-run on unrelated writes (measured: the lock toggle counted 3, not 2, and the first paint carried two spurious runs). The formatter's reads remain the dependencies. Framework-level, two lines, strictly fewer re-runs; the AC-2 counts are the control.
- **Immediate feedback is kept by publishing at the commit boundary**: a lock reaches its header, its pane and a revealed rail pane synchronously, as the deleted syncs did; the projection publishes once more, which is a no-op after a commit and the one publish a statically projected shell gets. The boot sweep in `afterSetMounted` and its tail-discipline machinery are deleted: with the first paint bound there is nothing to correct at mount.
- **A leaf a binding reads exists before the binding's first run**: `dock.flights.<id>` is seeded `null` per item, `dock.items.<id>.reloadable` is published as the pane resolves — a `Config` created after a formatter ran is not one of its dependencies.
- **The "stale window" is closed**, and its test flipped: a retained pin action whose item the model moved to the center refuses at the commit boundary. Dispatch still decides from the document.
- **Witnesses retired with their mechanism**: the four boot-sweep unit arms and the sweep witness classes, `DockBootSweep.spec`'s overlap arm and the `dock-static-boot-overlap` fixture app, the counting policy in `dock-static-boot`; `DockLayoutAdapter.spec` pins the dock's `TabContainer` as the projected module. Two latent spec facts fixed in passing: `DockSplitterLivePreview.spec` resolved the adapter off the namespace without importing it (red when run alone, at dev too), and a hand-built Workstation stub in `DockRecreateCandidate.spec` now declares it owns no provider.
- **Closure delta, declared**: single-window dock consumers now carry `state/Provider.mjs`, `core/Effect.mjs`, `core/EffectManager.mjs`, `state/createHierarchicalDataProxy.mjs` and the dock `TabContainer` (+4 modules net) — the binding primitive the ticket asks for; the Workstation, which already had the provider stack, grows by the one new class.
- `LayoutAdapter.project` gains three options (`dockHeaderActionBindings`, `dockNodeLockBinding`, `dockRailLockBinding`) and `dockWorkspaceId`; `syncDockLockPane` keeps its name and presents a reveal pane from published truth; `onDockActiveIndexChange`'s no-commit branch publishes the header's active item (one self-diffing leaf).
